newsitem.title: USA: Prosecution ends closing argument in Oklahoma case.
newsitem.headline: Prosecution ends closing argument in Oklahoma case.

text.p: The prosecution ended its closing argument on Thursday in the Oklahoma City bombing trial with an emotional appeal for the jury to convict accused bomber Timothy McVeigh, calling him "a man whose intent was to kill anyone and everyone and then run away."
The closing argument by prosecutor Larry Mackey lasted about three hours and 15 minutes. The defence's closing argument was slated for the afternoon court session.
Mackey reminded the jury of the 168 people who died in the blast and said McVeigh had created a "new grievance" against the victims and the nation as a whole.

"It has been our pleasure to represent those victims and the United States in settling that grievance," he said. "We have done so in a way Timothy McVeigh would not choose. We have done so through due process."
"Your privilege as well as your job is to do justice." he said to the jurors. "I ask you to return a verdict of guilty as charged against Timothy McVeigh."
McVeigh, 29, is charged with murder and conspiracy. If convicted, he faces the death penalty.
